subject: Post-call: Secure provisioning & key handover plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@atlashealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Secure provisioning & key handover plan

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

Key pain points you described
- Regulated PHI workflows: data must remain in Atlas VPC (no egress to public models).
- Strict KMS requirements: Atlas controls keys via an HSM-backed KMS; Redwoods’ private deployment must support customer-managed key handover and key rotation policies.
- Network constraints: outbound connections are highly restricted, and any external endpoints must be pre-authorized (firewall + proxy).
- Air-gap and deployment windows: potential air-gapped environments for higher-sensitivity workloads and long procurement lead times.

Current stack you shared
- On-prem Kubernetes (EKS Anywhere in some sites) + private Docker registry
- Internal HSM (Azure Key Vault Managed HSM for some regions; Thales in others)
- Centralized observability (Splunk) and internal SIEM ingestion

Success criteria (from your team)
1) No plaintext PHI leaves customer VPC during inference; logs are scrubbed and meet retention policies.
2) KMS integration with customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) with clear attestation and rotation process.
3) Ability to run a 2-week PoC in a staging environment that mimics production latency with a capped token budget.
4) Auditability: access logs, traceability per request, and SOC2 / pen test evidence.

Immediate asks / next steps (owners & ETA)
- Atlas: send updated network topology and list of IP ranges + proxy rules (owner: Tom) — requested by Fri 04/30. [Attachment: atlas_network_topology_v2.pdf (PDF)]
- Redwood (Monica): draft PoA for private deployment and KMS handover steps + rough infra sizing for PoC — EOD Mon 05/03. [Attachment: rwi-private-poa.pdf (PDF)]
- Atlas: confirm list of regulatory controls we should include in the audit checklist (owner: Sara) — Tue 05/04.
- Both: schedule a 90-minute technical deep-dive to validate firewall rules, KMS APIs (KMIP / REST), and required endpoints — propose Wed 05/05 or Thu 05/06.

Notes / constraints from our side
- Our default private package supports AWS KMS and Vault integrations; for HSM-backed on-prem KMS we’ll need certificate exchange and mutual TLS.
- Air-gap installs add ~4–6 weeks to provisioning depending on hardware validation and acceptance testing.

I’ve attached an initial private deployment plan (rwi-private-poa.pdf) that covers handover steps, cert expectations, and a draft rollback/validation checklist.

Thanks again — will follow up with Monica’s PoA and available deep-dive slots.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

[Attachment: rwi-private-poa.pdf (PDF)]

From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@atlashealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@atlashealth.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Secure provisioning & key handover plan

Vivek —

Thanks for the concise summary, that matches our notes. A few clarifications from the security team: 

1) KMS integration: we need to understand whether Redwood can support KMIP for our Thales HSMs, or whether we need to front a REST wrapper. If KMIP is supported, what versions and cipher suites do you require?

2) Remote attestation: for the air-gapped option we need attestation artifacts (signed measurements) back to our compliance team. Is there an automated attestation export in the private package or is that custom?

3) Network: I attached an updated topology with segmentation labels — Tom will finish the proxy ACL list by Friday.

4) PoC success criteria: for the PoC we’d like to include a performance gate (p95 inference latency < 250ms for a 128-token gen) and a small production smoke test that runs a subset of daily jobs against masked PHI. Can Redwood instrument per-request tracing to send metadata to our Splunk instance?

Attaching the topology file. We can do Wed 05/05 10:00-11:30 PT for the technical deep-dive — please confirm.

Sara Jensen
Director, InfoSec | Atlas Health Systems
sara.jensen@atlashealth.com | +1 (617) 222-9987

[Attachment: atlas_network_topology_v2.pdf (PDF)]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Atlas PoC - proposed infra & KMS workflow (do not forward)

Vivek / Dev —

Internal notes after the call / Sara’s reply. High level PoC proposal we can present on Wed: 

PoC topology (staging)
- 2-node GPU pool (A100 or H100 equivalence) behind customer VPC private subnet.
- Inference runtime in container with KV cache disabled for initial run (to simplify attestation).
- Sidecar connector for KMS: we propose a mutual-TLS REST shim to the customer Thales HSM (KMIP adapters are possible but we’ve had fewer integration surprises with an authenticated REST wrapper).

KMS handover flow (draft)
1) Cert exchange: Atlas provides public cert, Redwood generates CSR for module signing, both stored in customer Vault (customer-controlled).
2) Key provisioning: Atlas provisions keys into the HSM, Redwood pulls key handles via authenticated API; no key material is exported.
3) Rotations: rotation driven by Atlas; Redwood will accept rotated keys keyed by handle mapping and will log rotation events to the local audit log (immutable).
4) Attestation: we can produce signed measurement artifacts if we run on enclaves (SGX or Nitro Enclaves), else offer a package of hash-signed binaries and runtime checksums — need to confirm preference.

Instrumentation & observability
- Per-request tracing: can emit X-Request-ID and forward metadata to Atlas Splunk (via HTTPS forwarder) — need endpoint and token.
- Audit logs: delivery via secure syslog or S3 push to Atlas-controlled bucket (TLS + signed delivery).

Risk / open questions
- Air-gap approach: hardware manifests will need validation by our onsite engineer; expect 4–6 week hardware validation window.
- KMIP support: if they insist on KMIP we’ll scope an adapter; timeline +2 weeks.

Immediate internal asks
- Dev: prepare a short demo container that uses REST shim and logs request IDs (can reuse existing shim from FinTeam PoC).
- Vivek: confirm Wed 05/05 10:00 PT slot with Atlas and share invite; include our infra engineer (Ben Carter?) and legal if procurement discussions start.

I’ll package this into a 1-pager we can present.

— Monica
Monica Patel | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@atlashealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@atlashealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Secure provisioning & key handover plan

Sara / Tom —

Confirmed: Wed 05/05 10:00-11:30 PT works for our team. I’ve added Monica and Dev from infra; Ben Carter (infra lead) will join from Redwood as well. Calendar invite to follow.

Action summary & owners before the call
- Tom (Atlas): final proxy/ACL list and any egress rules + confirmation of Thales firmware version — due Tue 05/04.
- Sara (Atlas): confirm attestation preference (enclave signed artifacts vs binary hashes) and Splunk forwarder token/endpoint — due Tue 05/04.
- Monica (Redwood): finalize PoA + proposed mutual-TLS flow and demo container — due Mon 05/03 (attaching the PoA here).
- Dev/Ben (Redwood): prepare REST shim demo and check KMIP adapter feasibility — internal due Mon 05/03.

We’ll use the deep-dive to validate the network allowlist (no external DNS lookups during PoC), exchange certs, and walk through a sample request with tracing enabled. Post-call we’ll capture a short runbook for the PoC acceptance gate.

If there are contractual items that procurement wants ahead of the PoC (NDA addendum, BAA), please loop in procurement@atlashealth.com and I’ll pull Legal on our side.

Looking forward — Vivek
